memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Do not use dishonest standards when measuring length, weight or quantity. Use honest scales and honest weights, an honest ephah and an honest hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt.'" - Lev 19:35-36 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Weights and measures. Of all the things to close a chapter with, God chooses the accuracy of a merchant's scales.

In the ancient world this was easy to manipulate. Carry two sets of weights — a heavier one for buying, a lighter one for selling — and skim a small profit from every transaction. Nobody could tell. The difference was too small to notice, and it added up quietly over years.

God notices. The LORD detests dishonest scales, but accurate weights find favour with him (Prov 11:1). Detests is a strong word for something so small.

Because it is never really about the scales. It is about whether a person can be trusted when trust cannot be verified.

Our version is different but the principle is identical. The invoice with an extra hour on it. The expenses claim rounded generously upward. The work hours logged but not worked. The product described more favourably than it deserves.

And look at how God signs off: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt. The God of the exodus cares about your invoicing. The great Redeemer is concerned with your weights and measures.

Nothing is too small to be part of your walk with Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where are you slightly less than honest in ways nobody could verify?
2. Would your business or work practices survive God's inspection?
3. What does it mean that the God of the exodus cares about small honesty?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, make me honest where no one can check. Let my work and my dealings be clean, because You who redeemed me care about every detail. Amen.
